title: conv3x3-engine-zynq: runtime-programmable 3x3 convolution engine and fixed Sobel core for Zynq-7020
description:
Artifacts for a runtime-programmable 3x3 convolution engine (AXI4-Stream data path, AXI4-Lite register file with 18 signed 8-bit coefficients) and a fixed Sobel reference core targeting the AMD/Xilinx XC7Z020-1: Verilog RTL, self-checking testbenches with randomized AXI4-Stream backpressure, a fixed-point reference model, Vivado 2026.1 out-of-context scripts, and post-route utilization, timing and power reports at 148.5 MHz for line widths of 160, 1920 and 3840 pixels with distributed-RAM and block-RAM line buffers, plus AMD Vitis Vision filter2D and Sobel baselines on the same part and flow. Simulation covers 55 runs and 32 million pixels at 160x120, 1920x16 and 1920x1080, including full-rate input, mid-frame kernel rewrites, multi-frame sequences under adversarial backpressure, and the block-RAM variant.

Scope. The RTL is a reconstruction written from the design description after the original sources were lost. All hardware figures are post-route, out-of-context Vivado results; power is a vectorless estimate; no board-level runtime experiments were executed. At a 1920-pixel line width both cores meet 148.5 MHz with default implementation directives; at 3840 pixels only the block-RAM engine variant does. The BSDS500 edge-quality evaluation (fixed point vs float64, 200 test images, relaxed matching) was re-implemented and is included with a sensitivity study over the normalization shift and kernel family, as is a script reproducing the DDR feasibility-model tables. See README.md for details.
